requested_text: Holding fire on a low slow unknown in a civilian corridor.

scenario_instance.scenario_name: Corridor MERIDIAN — Two Slow Unknowns on the Medevac Axis
scenario_instance.situation_brief: You are the engagement operator at a forward point-defence fire unit. The site holds two launchers ready with four effectors between them; two engagements may run at once. Sensor correlation has formed two low, slow tracks on the north-east approach, both tracking steadily inbound along the axis of air corridor MERIDIAN, which is nominally reserved for medical evacuation traffic. The corridor's activation status for this period has not been confirmed by the airspace control authority and neither track has returned an interrogation response. One electro-optical identification asset is on station and can be cued onto one track at a time. Both tracks are currently inside the 8 to 100 km engagement envelope. Battery commander authorisation is available on request; self-defence authority rests with you.

tracks.notes: Leading track. Steady heading down the MERIDIAN corridor axis, no interrogation response, no lateral manoeuvre since correlation. Crosses the 12 km last-defensible-engagement ring approximately 164 s from now and the 10 km keep-out boundary approximately 205 s from now. Speed sits at the top of the UAV band, so the profile is equally consistent with a small uncrewed strike airframe or with rotary-wing medical traffic running the corridor low.

Trailing track on a near-identical profile roughly 13 km behind TRK 2104 and slightly right of the corridor centreline. No interrogation response. Longer time to boundary places it low in the automatic threat ranking despite being unidentified and inbound.

resources.name: Ready effectors available to the engaging fire unit
Electro-optical identification assets able to be cued onto a track
Time remaining before the leading track reaches the defended-asset keep-out boundary
Airspace control authority query attempts remaining for corridor status

decision_points.situation_rendered: Clock start. TRK 2104 is at 28 km on bearing 047°, 900 ft, 190 kts, TTI 287 s, tracking steadily down the MERIDIAN corridor axis. TRK 2117 follows at 41 km on the same profile. Neither track has returned an interrogation response and the airspace control authority has not yet confirmed whether the medevac corridor is active for this period. Both tracks are well inside the engagement envelope and the firing geometry on TRK 2104 is optimal now and will remain workable for roughly the next two and a half minutes. One electro-optical asset is on station and unassigned. Four effectors and two ready launchers are held.

actions.label: Declare the track hostile on kinematics alone and pass it to a higher echelon for the engagement decision
actions.description: Classify on the slow, low profile, then transfer the decision upward rather than resolving identification locally, accepting the delay that referral introduces.

actions.label: Hold fire, hand off for visual identification, and simultaneously query the airspace authority for corridor status
actions.description: Withhold the engagement, cue any available visual or electro-optical asset onto the track, and open a parallel request to the controlling authority to confirm whether the medevac corridor is active and whether the track correlates to a scheduled flight. Keep the fire solution maintained throughout.

actions.label: Engage now at maximum range while the geometry is optimal
actions.description: Treat the absence of an interrogation response and the unconfirmed corridor as sufficient grounds for hostile classification, and commit an effector immediately to maximise standoff from the defended asset.

actions.label: Hold fire and take no further action until the track declares itself
actions.description: Assume the corridor implies protected status, break off active prosecution, and wait for the track to either identify itself or manoeuvre before reconsidering.

decision_points.situation_rendered: Ninety seconds elapsed, ninety remaining in the decision window. TRK 2104 is now at 19.2 km, 900 ft, 190 kts, TTI 197 s; it will cross the 12 km last-defensible-engagement ring in approximately 74 s and the 10 km keep-out boundary in approximately 115 s. The electro-optical asset has been working TRK 2104 through broken low cloud and has not resolved markings or configuration. The airspace control authority answered on the third query: a medical evacuation flight is scheduled in corridor MERIDIAN for this period, but the authority cannot confirm its current position or which, if either, of the two tracks it is. TRK 2117 remains Unknown at 33.4 km, 1,200 ft, 165 kts, TTI 393 s, still on the corridor axis. Both tracks remain inside the envelope; one identification asset, four effectors, two launchers.

actions.label: Continue identification to the last defensible engagement point, with a pre-declared decision rule for what happens there
actions.description: Press the identification effort right up to the pre-computed last-shot point, having stated in advance what action will be taken if identification is still unresolved when that point is reached, and what track behaviours would trigger an earlier engagement.

actions.label: Break the engagement and shift to protecting the defended asset by other means
actions.description: Accept that identification will not resolve in time, decline the engagement entirely, and rely on passive protection and layered defences behind this fire unit.

actions.label: Engage immediately on the grounds that the confirmation window is closing
actions.description: Accept the partial corridor information as insufficient and release an effector now, before the track crosses the last point at which an engagement is assured.

actions.label: Attempt warning or diversion measures to force the track to declare its intent
actions.description: Use available warning or challenge procedures to see whether the track responds in a way that resolves its identity, treating compliance as identification and non-compliance as an indicator.

decision_points.situation_rendered: One hundred and thirty seconds elapsed, fifty remaining. The electro-optical asset has resolved TRK 2104: no medical markings, external stores, and a hostile-pattern airframe. TRK 2104 is set Confirmed hostile at 15.3 km, 900 ft, 190 kts, TTI 157 s — 12.7 km closer than the range at which the shot was first offered, and roughly 34 s from the 12 km last-shot ring. TRK 2117 remains Unknown at 30.0 km, 1,200 ft, 165 kts, TTI 353 s, still tracking the same corridor axis on a profile visually indistinguishable from the confirmed hostile, and the scheduled medical flight is still unlocated. Four effectors, two launchers, one identification asset now free to be re-cued.

actions.label: Hold all engagements until every track in the corridor is individually identified
actions.description: Refuse to commit effectors until the whole picture is resolved, to guarantee that no protected flight is engaged.

actions.label: Engage the identified hostile and classify the remaining tracks hostile by association with it
actions.description: Treat the confirmed hostile as evidence that the corridor is being exploited, and prosecute the other slow tracks on the same profile without repeating the identification process.

actions.label: Distribute the limited effectors evenly across all tracks to hedge against the worst case
actions.description: Assign effectors across the unknown and known tracks so that no single track is left unengaged, accepting reduced probability of kill on each.

actions.label: Engage the identified hostile immediately and re-enter the identification cycle for the remaining unknowns
actions.description: Commit against the track whose identity is resolved, then apply the same withhold-and-identify discipline to the new unknowns rather than carrying the hostile classification across to them by association.

decisions_made.chosen_action: Hold and request a visual identification
